items.title: Up over 200% in 1 year, what's buzzing with Borosil Glass?
items.summary: Shares of Borosil Glass Works have increased threefold over the past one year as the company has posted strong revenue and EBIDTA growth over the past few quarters.

items.title: Why you should not be always chasing returns
items.summary: Most people focus on returns and chase products that offer the best returns at any point.

items.title: Jhunjhunwala-partnered fund buys stake in TFCI: What's buzzing?
items.summary: In an interview with CNBC-TV18, Satpal Arora, MD of Tourism Finance Corporation of India (TFCI), talked about the state of business and the outlook ahead.

items.title: RBI latest meeting 'diluted' its old policy framework: Nomura
items.summary: On Tuesday, the central bank surprised the market with a 25-basis-point cut to its policy repo rate, or the rate at which it lends to banks, to 6.25 percent.

items.title: Bond bull market may pause but is far from over: Expert
items.summary: The benchmark 10-year government-security yield remained stuck in 8-7.5 percent range through all of 2015 and half of 2016, moving lower to sub-7 percent only when the RBI promised in April to reduce the system's liquidity deficit. The yield may now fall more.

items.title: Scope for meaningful rate cuts going ahead: Neelkanth Mishra
items.summary: Credit Suisse' Neelkanth Mishra expects repo rate to fall to a decade low in the coming quarters. He says that beginning December the market may see a robust and widespread pick-up which may boost indices.

items.title: Tech up to a healthier world
items.summary: Sensors, 3D printed skin, wearables, reconstructed organs, revolutionized clinical trials, personalized medicine and what not – get ready for a new era of healthcare

items.title: Steel stocks rally as govt extends MIP on 66 steel products
items.summary: Stocks like Hindustan Zinc, Hindalco, Jindal Steel, JSW Steel and Tata Steel gained over 1 percent from previous close.

items.title: Endurance Technologies IPO opens: Should you subscribe?
items.summary: The Aurangabad-based company aims to mop up nearly Rs 1,162 crore (at higher end of price band) by diluting 17.5 percent stake through the issue that will close on October 7. It already raised Rs 348.52 crore through anchor investors' portion on Tuesday, the day before issue opening.

items.title: Cautiously optimistic on India; eyeing earnings revival: Sanger
items.summary: Global liquidity tailwinds are unlikely to get any better from now and that makes Arvind Sanger, Managing Partner at Geosphere Capital Management “cautiously optimistic” on the Indian markets.

items.title: Automation threatens 69% jobs in India: World Bank
items.summary: "In large parts of Africa, it is likely that technology could fundamentally disrupt this pattern. Research based on World Bank data has predicted that the proportion of jobs threatened in India by automation is 69 percent, in China it is 77 percent and in Ethiopia, the percentage of jobs threatened by automation is 85 percent," he said.

items.title: Why the Global South needs its own shared space architecture
items.summary: Over-reliance on Western commercial satellites leaves developing nations exposed during geopolitical crises, making a sovereign public network essential for long-term security.

items.title: Trade agreements don't guarantee an export boost—here's what exporters should do to make the most of FTAs
items.summary: It would be a mistake to assume that a free trade agreement automatically results in trade gains for Indian exporters. Exporters must work on productivity and reliability. They also need low-cost ways to comply with complex regulatory requirements abroad.

items.title: Student expectations of the Nikelani panel are high but education needs far more than exam reforms
items.summary: A new panel headed by Infosys chairman Nandan Nilekani has raised hopes of this sector’s reform. Yet, India faces such steep challenges that it’s likely nothing short of a system-wide overhaul will do. Here are some cues for consideration.

items.title: Sports associations like Fifa must pay taxes—their tournaments are clearly big business for them
items.summary: There is no reason why sports bodies like Fifa and BCCI should not pay all their taxes. They derive enormous financial benefits from infrastructure built mostly with the money of taxpayers. And Fifa’s 2026 World Cup is set to smash revenue records.

items.title: OpenAI models hacked Hugging Face: human minds must figure out how to make the world safer
items.summary: Fears of rogue artificial intelligence (AI) were revived last week by news of OpenAI’s models escaping their testing enclosures to hack another firm’s digital systems. How to optimize controls is a stiff challenge, but here’s what might work.

items.title: Nolan’s ‘The Odyssey’ shows that the loudest critics don’t always represent the majority view
items.summary: Despite heavy online criticism from some moviegoers, Christopher Nolan’s take on Homer’s epic has broken box office records. Hollywood studios that bow to online voices need a lesson in statistics 101: every sample isn’t representative.

items.title: Nitin Pai: Biotech offers India a shot at global leadership—here's what must be done to achieve it
items.summary: For the country to remain the 'pharmacy of the world,' it must overcome the squeeze of US tariffs and Chinese breakthroughs. To not just survive the future but thrive, we need an overhaul of how the biotech industry is governed.

items.title: Nageswaran: Open weight AI has already diffused across the world—with dangers we must act upon
items.summary: Sure, open weight models put AI capability in far more hands than proprietary tools do. Yet, such easily available models can also help create biological weapons. We need a global control apparatus like the one set up against nuclear threats.

items.title: Mint Quick Edit | When will Indian stocks look up again? An end to this year’s oil shock will help
items.summary: India Inc’s last-quarter earnings hold promise while economic conditions show signs of improvement, but the war in West Asia has cast a shadow on market sentiment again. Investors need relief from energy-cost uncertainty.

items.title: Mint Quick Edit | Johnson & Johnson’s $5.5 billion offer to settle cancer-risk suits: is money enough?
items.summary: This American pharma major wants to end its nightmare of lawsuits over allegations of ovarian cancer-causing talcum powder. But its therapeutic advances—in oncology, especially—might determine whether it can rescue J&amp;J as a brand.

items.title: Mint Quick Edit | India’s education ministry has seen a shift—will market-inspired reforms follow?
items.summary: The ouster of a minister is one thing, reforms that align the country’s education system with the economy’s evolution are another. Here’s what India’s best bet might be in the face of today’s challenges.

items.title: Mint Quick Edit | ChangXi’s listing pop was an eye-popper: can Indian chipmakers reach the big league?
items.summary: Fervent investor interest in chipmaking successes is a sign of today’s tech-driven times. India’s Semiconductor Mission aims to develop local fabs and an entire ecosystem. Success, however, will take more than big money.

items.title: Manu Joseph: What ails the BJP’s relationship with India’s youth is not what it may look like
items.summary: For the first time, India’s ruling party is at risk of being cast in a mould from which there seems no escape. The failing promise of higher education has left young Indians in a foreseeable state of disaffection. And Indian society played a role in it.

items.title: Major League Baseball wants AI kept out of the dugout—but that’s a pointless effort
items.summary: With artificial intelligence entering ballparks, critics are concerned the game will turn into a battle of engineers. But data analytics reshaped baseball long ago, as Michael Lewis explained in his classic ‘Moneyball.’ AI simply can’t be kept out of dugouts.

items.title: KM Mammen Mappillai: the man who built MRF from a balloon shed
items.summary: From a tiny balloon unit in Chennai to India's largest tyre maker, KM Mammen Mappillai built MRF through engineering, discipline and an unwavering belief in Indian manufacturing.

items.title: India’s order against Bitchat defies logic—and it’s time to draw a clear line on software bans
items.summary: Can the capacity to escape state surveillance be interpreted as an offence in itself? India's action directed at Bitchat reveals muddled thinking on basic principles. While the digital sector awaits clarity, Bitchat benefits from the Streisand effect.

items.title: India's research and development ecosystem is in need a major overhaul. Here's why
items.summary: To compete at a global level amid rapid technological advances, the country must spread research out and place post-doctoral researchers at the heart of its R&amp;D ecosystem. Policymakers need to press a restart button.

items.title: I nearly fired my AI chatbot yesterday
items.summary: The more we collaborate with AI, the more we expect it to behave like a colleague

items.title: Global trends show a relative decline in self-employment as a country ascends income brackets
items.summary: For India to achieve upper middle-income status by 2047, it needs a substantial employment shift in favour of formal jobs. For that to happen, employers of all sizes—small, medium and large—must grow.

items.title: Get the nitty-gritty right: the impact of RBI's data governance proposals will depend on finer details
items.summary: The central bank’s Guidance on Regulatory Expectations for Data Governance is timely, given the need for greater discipline in data usage by banks and NBFCs. Public consultations would be needed to get the details right—and some trade-offs will need to be made.

items.title: Forced labour is America’s latest pretext for a policy that mustn’t escape internal checks and balances
items.summary: As US trade barriers pivot from one law to another for support, the odds of judicial relief seem steeper this time round—but must not weaken. Nor can India flatly deny the warts and woes of its labour market.

items.title: Fashion fight: a Japanese rival may be emerging to challenge Spain’s Zara and China's Shein
items.summary: Fast Retailing's GU is a cheaper and trendier brand than its big success Uniqlo. And it has something that could give global fast fashion majors a run for its money. Zara and Shein had better watch out.

items.title: Electrifying progress: shipping may take time to dump fossil fuels but ports are switching to clean energy
items.summary: The global transition to clean energy has found safe harbour in an unlikely place—ports. Although ships may run on carbon-spewing fuels for quite a while yet, the land operations of shipping are going electric. It counts as climate action.

items.title: Donald Trump’s Saudi deal risks nuclear proliferation
items.summary: The deal with Saudi Arabia that President Donald Trump announced on July 22nd would not even qualify as bronze. The text has yet to be published, but if leaks are accurate, it will firm up America’s twitchy relations with the kingdom and be lucrative for American companies.

items.title: Dhiraj Nim: India's Goldilocks era may be on its way out—here's what the numbers say
items.summary: Does India’s recent phase of puzzlingly low inflation amid robust GDP growth have an explanation? It does. And it’s also why that run of disinflation was extraordinary and offers policymakers no comfort on price stability from here on.

items.title: Companies that depend too heavily on just a few employees risk handicapping themselves
items.summary: Nearly every organization has a handful of employees who are entrusted with vital tasks beyond their formal job roles and end up carrying the weight of entire teams. Over-reliance on such individuals can make firms complacent and lose focus on capability diffusion.

items.title: Census 2027: raise its credibility through a consensus on how castes are best enumerated
items.summary: Lack of clarity over the questionnaire for caste enumeration in India’s headcount is a matter of concern. The demand for it has been there for decades. A recent effort was open-ended and had stumbled on caste nomenclature. Don’t repeat the error.

items.title: Capitalism’s status hierarchy is being upturned
items.summary: Capitalism’s status-industrial complex has been upturned, as institutions such as universities and newspapers that once conferred prestige lose their power to do so.

items.title: Can India lead the world’s middle powers? Indian democracy would need to be strengthened first
items.summary: Stronger institutions and greater respect for human rights would make it easier for New Delhi to rally other nations together that share India’s global concerns. The country’s democracy quotient is a key determinant of the strength of its global voice.

items.title: Artificial wisdom does not exist—but is this clear to everyone? A jobs crisis may be the smaller threat
items.summary: The worry of human employment compression as AI takes over job roles may be less of a challenge than this technology’s impact on the ‘wisdom of crowds.’ If independent judgement ends up as AI’s first profound casualty, it would fail humanity.

items.title: American air fares will likely stay at an incline as budget carriers wobble and premium flying soars
items.summary: Airlines in the US can no longer afford to compete on price, given the effect of war-fired fuel bills. While budget carriers in the US stare at trouble, other carriers are adding frills to justify premium fares. Is the era of low-cost flying over?

items.title: All newborns must be screened for congenital hypothyroidism—well before its effects show up
items.summary: Indian children are more susceptible than others to congenital hypothyroidism, which can impair mental development if not caught early. To detect it at a stage when its impact can wholly be prevented, screening of newborns at scale is a must—by policy.

items.title: Ajit Ranade: Here are five lessons for India from China's successful higher education strategy
items.summary: Street protests triggered by NEET paper leaks have drawn attention to the need for educational reform, but India must look beyond instilling trust in state-run competitive exams. What China has pulled off as part of a strategic mission deserves a close look.

items.title: A students stir of 1990 may hold lessons for those who hit the streets to protest exam paper leaks
items.summary: As CJP-led protestors celebrate the exit of India’s former education minister, they must learn from a youth movement of an earlier generation. What India needs done for grievance redressal is expansive—and mustn’t get lost in the noise of politics.

items.title: A digital transformation has put India on a firm path to its goal of ‘developed country’ status by 2047
items.summary: India has taken big leaps in digital adoption that have spurred financial inclusion, transformed service delivery to citizens and geared the economy up for it to meet its 2047 goal. But we must ensure that citizens possess the digital skills needed to benefit from all this.
